title: Burst-tolerant admission controller with KV tiering and GPU slab-aware slot leasing
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS with frequent short bursts we observe repeating tail-latency spikes and transient GPU OOMs. Root cause signals include aggressive KV cache churn (hot-keys cycling between GPU and host), a fixed micro-batch admission threshold that oscillates under sharp arrival-rate changes, and lack of a graceful degrade path for small, latency-sensitive requests.

Goal: Implement a burst-tolerant admission controller that combines per-tenant token-slot leasing driven by GPU slab occupancy, a small speculative fast-path admission for sub-50-token requests, and a multi-tier KV cache policy that evicts cold entries asynchronously to host and compacts hot shards without blocking the serving path. The controller should avoid oscillatory behavior, preserve tail latency SLOs (P99), and reduce transient GPU memory pressure while maintaining overall throughput.

Non-goals: Rewriting the entire KV persistence layer, adding new hardware types, or changing model quantization schemes in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Sustained run (48h) under synthetic mixed traffic (steady 10k rps + intermittent 50k rps bursts) shows P99 latency improvement >=25% compared to baseline and <1% request error rate due to OOM.
2) GPU free memory headroom metric no longer drops below configured critical threshold during bursts.
3) KV hit-rate degradation limited to <5% during bursts; background spill/compaction does not increase tail latency.
4) Feature behind runtime feature-flag; canary rollout to 10% of serving pool with automated rollback on breach of SLOs.
notes:
Key ideas discussed in design review (2026-02-22): use GPU slab occupancy as a primary signal for admission rate; prefer short speculative admits for <=50 token requests (fast-path) that bypass batching if headroom exists; implement a soft-leaky per-tenant slot bucket with exponential backoff on refusal; background compaction threads to migrate cold KV pages to host and explicit hot-shard pinning for tenants with priority traffic.

Trade-offs: The speculative fast-path reduces batching efficiency for a subset of requests but significantly improves P95/P99 for latency-sensitive calls. Per-tenant leasing avoids global oscillation but needs tight accounting to prevent starvation of low-priority tenants.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for slot-leasing algorithm and GPU-occupancy listener.
2) Integration test harness with synthetic workloads (Poisson baseline + Pareto bursts) to validate non-oscillation and fairness.
3) Chaos test: simulate KV page degradation and forced host spills to validate background compactor behavior.
4) Perf job in CI that measures P50/P95/P99, kv_hit_rate, gpu_free_bytes under benchmark traffic.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1: Feature-flagged deploy to staging with full telemetry and debug dumps (1 week).
Stage 2: Canary to 10% of production serving nodes for 48 hours; monitor P99, error-rate, gpu-headroom, kv_spill_rate.
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% with staggered tenant cohorts (by traffic profile).
Rollback criteria: P99 increases >10% from baseline or OOM-related errors appear.
metrics:
Primary: p99_latency_ms, gpu_free_bytes_ratio, kv_gpu_hit_rate, request_reject_rate, accepted_slots_per_minute.
Secondary: burst_recovery_time_seconds, per_tenant_fairness_index, background_compaction_throughput.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: New admission policy could unfairly throttle low-tier customers during long bursts. Mitigation: implement tenant-weighted minimum refill and emergency grace tokens for active sessions.
Risk: Background compaction might compete with serving threads. Mitigation: compaction runs with IO/cpu cgroups and uses incremental scheduling tied to gpu_free_bytes_ratio.

1) Finalize refill function constants (alpha/beta) after one week of canary telemetry.
2) Decide whether to expose per-tenant soft-prioritization to customers or keep as internal policy.
